tagline: A settlement by the Kentucky River, rebuilt in timber.
intro: The trail reaches the Kentucky River at Boonesborough, where Daniel Boone and his men crossed on April 1, 1775, and built a fort. Kentucky's first representative government met here that May, and by summer the place had 26 one-story log cabins and four blockhouses.

The fort held through the Great Siege of September 1778. Afterward it was a stop for westward-bound settlers and the tobacco trade, and by 1820 it had ceased to matter much. In the park, the old Lock 10 operator's home now holds the Kentucky River Museum.

moments.title: Boonesborough
moments.text: Boone lived here from 1775 to 1779, but the town never kept many people for long, and by 1877 it had almost disappeared as a village.

moments.title: Fort Boonesborough State Park
moments.text: The reproduction fort has cabins, bunkhouses, and furnishings, and in season resident blacksmiths and potters work in the open for visitors.
